# Review of beowulf-fitt-12 (lines 791–836)

`t`, `ln`, `v`, `p` checked byte-identical before and after (script assert over all 18 units). All note lengths after editing are 66–132 words (limit 150). Edits to `units.json` and `gloss.json` were made by script.

## Line numbers cited from other parts, verified against source/beowulf-klaeber1922.json and the published parts

All correct: 312 hildedēor; 429 wīgendra hlēo; 710 misthleoþum; 718 aldordagum; 720 sīðian; 721 drēamum bedǣled; 726 him of ēagum stōd; 732 atol āglǣca (spelled ā); 733 ālumpen; 742 bāt bānlocan; 743 synsnǣdum; 767 "Denum eallum wearð" (the frame opens in 767; "ealuscerwen" itself is in 769, which the note does not claim otherwise); 787 sār wānigean; 790 on þǣm dæge þysses līfes; 86 ellengǣst (added by me, fitt I); 147 twelf wintra (added); 432 Heorot fǣlsian (added); 407 and 736 Higelāces mǣg (added). No fix was needed to any cited number. The only cited-line problems were in what the note said about 767 (see 823 below).

## Pass 1: findings considered and refused

- ‘eorl Bēowulfes’ as a collective (794): kept; the plural ‘hīe meahton’ supports it, and l stays literal.
- ‘wearð … gyfeþe’ called a passive (818): kept; "became granted" = "was granted", acceptable.
- ‘ǣglǣca … also to heroes’ (815): kept; the published fitt II note already says the poem later applies it to Beowulf.
- ‘mōdes myrðe’ "with relish" (809): kept; it is flagged as a guess and the Gering variant is given.
- ‘forswerian’ sense (804): kept as a flagged guess.
- ‘frēadrihtnes’ as "master-lord" (794): kept; a new but transparent compound of ‘frēa’ + ‘dryhten’, no house rendering exists.
- "sick unto death" (819): kept; it translates ‘feorhsēoc’ directly and is not a recalled translation.
- First dot under a vowel (‘mōdẹga’, 809): correctly the first in this part and explained there.
- Section 805 "Should" in l: kept as literal; i says "was to".
- ‘hildedēor’ "compare 312" (833): correct.

| unlȳtel (broaden) | gloss.json | medium | "accusative singular masculine, with torn"; ‘torn’ is neuter and the form is the uninflected one. | "accusative singular, uninflected neuter form, in apposition …". |

| nytte, gewin, grāpe, hlēo, bānlocan, cyst | gloss.json (__broaden__) | low (6) | Existing entries did not cover this use: nytte as adjective; gewin as accusative object; grāpe as nominative/appositive (Grendles grāpe); hlēo as subject, not address; bānlocan nominative plural; cyst nominative. | Added under `__broaden__`, old entry whole + " · " + new reading. |

Checked and found true: all other novel-form parses (case, number, gender, tense, verb class) against the lines; the five other broaden entries (þē, sele, ende, god, and unlȳtel after fix); the known-form entries not listed above.

## Pass 2: findings considered and refused

- ‘gūðhrēð’ masculine and ‘healfa gehwone’ (feminine noun with masculine pronoun): left as the glosser wrote; the lexica are not decisive and the sense is unaffected.
- ‘ǣnigum’ "dative singular masculine": kept; singular or plural gives the same sense.
- ‘ellorgāst’ "alien spirit" in the gloss: kept; it is a lexicon-style meaning, not idiomatic English in a line.
- ‘Hygelāc … uncle’: kept; the glosser's identification is not in these lines but is the standard one and does not affect any line.
- ‘sīðian’ "after cōm" (known entry): the remark is incidental; parse unaffected.
- ‘gebād’ "takes the genitive" (known entry): not contradicted here; left alone.
- Key ‘hygelāces’ spelled with y while published keys use the printed spelling: matches the printed form.
